steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	cd "$(dirname "$0")"
5	
6	HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$PWD/models/JustRL-II-base-model}
7	MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH=${MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH:-$PWD/models/JustRL-II-base-model-torch_dist}
8	RAW_DATA=${RAW_DATA:-$PWD/raw/countdown}
9	DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD/data/countdown}
10	OUT=${OUT:-${LOG_DIR:-$PWD/results/ppo_countdown}}
11	STEPS=${STEPS:-30}
12	SEED=${SEED:-42}
13	ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE=${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-16}
14	N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-4}
15	MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=${MICRO_BATCH_SIZE:-4}
16	NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS=${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-3}
17	EVAL_INTERVAL=${EVAL_INTERVAL:-10}
18	LR=${LR:-2e-6}
19	CRITIC_LR=${CRITIC_LR:-1e-5}
20	DISTRIBUTED_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=${DISTRIBUTED_TIMEOUT_MINUTES:-3}
21	MEGATRON_DIR=${MEGATRON_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}
22	SGLANG_DIR=${SGLANG_DIR:-/sgl-workspace/sglang}
23	
24	GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE=$((ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT))
25	
26	mkdir -p "$OUT" "$DATA_DIR"
27	
28	if [ ! -f "$DATA_DIR/train.jsonl" ] || [ ! -f "$DATA_DIR/test.jsonl" ]; then
29	  if [ -e "$RAW_DATA" ]; then
30	    python3 data_prep/countdown.py --src "$RAW_DATA" --out "$DATA_DIR" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/data_prep.log"
31	  else
32	    echo "FATAL: missing prepared $DATA_DIR/{train,test}.jsonl and RAW_DATA=$RAW_DATA" >&2
33	    exit 1
34	  fi
35	fi
36	
37	# Convert HF model -> Megatron torch_dist on first GPU run if prepare.sh ran CPU-only
38	if [ ! -d "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH/release" ] && [ ! -f "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
39	  echo "Converting HF model $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH ..."
40	  mkdir -p "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH"
41	  source justrl2/model_args/minicpm5-2b.sh
42	  HF_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1 \
43	  CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1 \
44	  NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1 \
45	  NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0 \
46	  NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN=0 \
47	  WORLD_SIZE=1 RANK=0 LOCAL_RANK=0 MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1 MASTER_PORT="${CONVERT_MASTER_PORT:-29365}" \
48	  PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${MEGATRON_DIR}:${SGLANG_DIR}/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" \
49	    python3 tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
50	      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
51	      --attention-backend fused \
52	      --no-gradient-accumulation-fusion \
53	      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
54	      --save "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/convert_model.log"
55	fi
56	
57	rm -f "$OUT/metrics.jsonl"
58	rm -rf "$OUT/val_generations"
59	mkdir -p "$OUT/val_generations"
60	
61	unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY no_proxy NO_PROXY ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
62	
63	export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${MEGATRON_DIR}:${SGLANG_DIR}/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
64	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
65	export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
66	export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
67	export HF_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1
68	export CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
69	export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
70	export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0
71	export NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN=0
72	export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
73	export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0
74	export TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=2000
75	export TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1
76	export TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC=60
77	export TORCH_NCCL_DEBUG_INFO_TEMP_FILE="$OUT/nccl_trace_rank_"
78	export WANDB_MODE=offline
79	export TENSORBOARD_DIR="$OUT/tensorboard"
80	export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
81	export MILES_EXPERIMENTAL_ROLLOUT_REFACTOR=0
82	export MILES_METRICS_FILE="$OUT/metrics.jsonl"
83	export MILES_EVAL_DUMP_DIR="$OUT/val_generations"
84	export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1
85	export TRITON_CACHE_DIR="${TRITON_CACHE_DIR:-/tmp/triton_cache_$$}"
86	export TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
87	mkdir -p "$TENSORBOARD_DIR" "$TRITON_CACHE_DIR"
88	
89	source justrl2/model_args/minicpm5-2b.sh
90	
91	RAY_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/justrl2-ray-XXXXXX)
92	cleanup() {
93	  ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
94	  rm -rf "$RAY_TMPDIR" "$TRITON_CACHE_DIR" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
95	}
96	trap cleanup EXIT
97	
98	RAY_PORT=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0)); p=s.getsockname()[1]; s.close(); print(p)')
99	ray start --head \
100	  --node-ip-address=127.0.0.1 \
101	  --port="$RAY_PORT" \
102	  --temp-dir="$RAY_TMPDIR" \
103	  --num-gpus=8 \
104	  --num-cpus=32 \
105	  --object-store-memory=8000000000 \
106	  --include-dashboard=false \
107	  --disable-usage-stats
108	
109	export RAY_ADDRESS="127.0.0.1:${RAY_PORT}"
110	
111	TRAIN_ENV_JSON=$(python3 -c '
112	import json, os
113	keys = [
114	    "PYTHONPATH", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM",
115	    "CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "NVTE_FUSED_ATTN", "NVTE_FLASH_ATTN", "NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN",
116	    "NCCL_DEBUG", "NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE",
117	    "TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE", "TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT",
118	    "TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC", "TORCH_NCCL_DEBUG_INFO_TEMP_FILE",
119	    "WANDB_MODE", "TENSORBOARD_DIR",
120	    "MILES_METRICS_FILE", "MILES_EVAL_DUMP_DIR",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

HF_MODEL_DIR=${HF_MODEL_DIR:-$PWD/models/JustRL-II-base-model}
MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH=${MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH:-$PWD/models/JustRL-II-base-model-torch_dist}
RAW_DATA=${RAW_DATA:-$PWD/raw/countdown}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD/data/countdown}
OUT=${OUT:-${LOG_DIR:-$PWD/results/ppo_countdown}}
STEPS=${STEPS:-30}
SEED=${SEED:-42}
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE=${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-16}
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-4}
MICRO_BATCH_SIZE=${MICRO_BATCH_SIZE:-4}
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS=${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-3}
EVAL_INTERVAL=${EVAL_INTERVAL:-10}
LR=${LR:-2e-6}
CRITIC_LR=${CRITIC_LR:-1e-5}
DISTRIBUTED_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=${DISTRIBUTED_TIMEOUT_MINUTES:-3}
MEGATRON_DIR=${MEGATRON_DIR:-/root/Megatron-LM}
SGLANG_DIR=${SGLANG_DIR:-/sgl-workspace/sglang}

GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE=$((ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT))

mkdir -p "$OUT" "$DATA_DIR"

if [ ! -f "$DATA_DIR/train.jsonl" ] || [ ! -f "$DATA_DIR/test.jsonl" ]; then
  if [ -e "$RAW_DATA" ]; then
    python3 data_prep/countdown.py --src "$RAW_DATA" --out "$DATA_DIR" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/data_prep.log"
  else
    echo "FATAL: missing prepared $DATA_DIR/{train,test}.jsonl and RAW_DATA=$RAW_DATA" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# Convert HF model -> Megatron torch_dist on first GPU run if prepare.sh ran CPU-only
if [ ! -d "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH/release" ] && [ ! -f "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
  echo "Converting HF model $HF_MODEL_DIR -> $MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH ..."
  mkdir -p "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH"
  source justrl2/model_args/minicpm5-2b.sh
  HF_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1 \
  CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1 \
  NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1 \
  NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0 \
  NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN=0 \
  WORLD_SIZE=1 RANK=0 LOCAL_RANK=0 MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1 MASTER_PORT="${CONVERT_MASTER_PORT:-29365}" \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${MEGATRON_DIR}:${SGLANG_DIR}/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" \
    python3 tools/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py \
      "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
      --attention-backend fused \
      --no-gradient-accumulation-fusion \
      --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
      --save "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/convert_model.log"
fi

rm -f "$OUT/metrics.jsonl"
rm -rf "$OUT/val_generations"
mkdir -p "$OUT/val_generations"

unset http_proxy HTTP_PROXY https_proxy HTTPS_PROXY no_proxy NO_PROXY ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES

export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${MEGATRON_DIR}:${SGLANG_DIR}/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export HF_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1
export CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
export NVTE_FUSED_ATTN=1
export NVTE_FLASH_ATTN=0
export NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN=0
export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0
export TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE=2000
export TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT=1
export TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC=60
export TORCH_NCCL_DEBUG_INFO_TEMP_FILE="$OUT/nccl_trace_rank_"
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export TENSORBOARD_DIR="$OUT/tensorboard"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0
export MILES_EXPERIMENTAL_ROLLOUT_REFACTOR=0
export MILES_METRICS_FILE="$OUT/metrics.jsonl"
export MILES_EVAL_DUMP_DIR="$OUT/val_generations"
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1
export TRITON_CACHE_DIR="${TRITON_CACHE_DIR:-/tmp/triton_cache_$$}"
export TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
mkdir -p "$TENSORBOARD_DIR" "$TRITON_CACHE_DIR"

source justrl2/model_args/minicpm5-2b.sh

RAY_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/justrl2-ray-XXXXXX)
cleanup() {
  ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$RAY_TMPDIR" "$TRITON_CACHE_DIR" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

RAY_PORT=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0)); p=s.getsockname()[1]; s.close(); print(p)')
ray start --head \
  --node-ip-address=127.0.0.1 \
  --port="$RAY_PORT" \
  --temp-dir="$RAY_TMPDIR" \
  --num-gpus=8 \
  --num-cpus=32 \
  --object-store-memory=8000000000 \
  --include-dashboard=false \
  --disable-usage-stats

export RAY_ADDRESS="127.0.0.1:${RAY_PORT}"

TRAIN_ENV_JSON=$(python3 -c '
import json, os
keys = [
    "PYTHONPATH", "OMP_NUM_THREADS", "TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM",
    "CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS", "NVTE_FUSED_ATTN", "NVTE_FLASH_ATTN", "NVTE_UNFUSED_ATTN",
    "NCCL_DEBUG", "NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE",
    "TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE", "TORCH_NCCL_DUMP_ON_TIMEOUT",
    "TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC", "TORCH_NCCL_DEBUG_INFO_TEMP_FILE",
    "WANDB_MODE", "TENSORBOARD_DIR",
    "MILES_METRICS_FILE", "MILES_EVAL_DUMP_DIR",
    "TRITON_CACHE_DIR", "TMPDIR",
]
print(json.dumps({k: os.environ[k] for k in keys if k in os.environ}))
')

python3 train.py \
  --actor-num-nodes 1 \
  --actor-num-gpus-per-node 4 \
  --critic-num-nodes 1 \
  --critic-num-gpus-per-node 4 \
  --num-gpus-per-node 8 \
  --colocate \
  --no-offload-train \
  --no-offload-rollout \
  --train-backend megatron \
  --tensor-model-parallel-size 1 \
  --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1 \
  --context-parallel-size 2 \
  --expert-model-parallel-size 1 \
  --expert-tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --qkv-format thd \
  --attention-backend fused \
  --no-gradient-accumulation-fusion \
  --recompute-granularity full \
  --recompute-method uniform \
  --recompute-num-layers 1 \
  --attention-dropout 0.0 \
  --hidden-dropout 0.0 \
  --log-probs-chunk-size -1 \
  "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
  --hf-checkpoint "$HF_MODEL_DIR" \
  --ref-load "$MEGATRON_MODEL_PATH" \
  --prompt-data "$DATA_DIR/train.jsonl" \
  --input-key prompt \
  --label-key label \
  --apply-chat-template \
  --apply-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
  --rollout-shuffle \
  --custom-rm-path reward.countdown_reward.compute_reward \
  --num-rollout "$STEPS" \
  --rollout-batch-size "$ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE" \
  --n-samples-per-prompt "$N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT" \
  --global-batch-size "$GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE" \
  --micro-batch-size "$MICRO_BATCH_SIZE" \
  --rollout-max-prompt-len 1024 \
  --rollout-max-response-len 512 \
  --rollout-max-context-len 2048 \
  --seq-length 2048 \
  --rollout-temperature 1.0 \
  --rollout-top-p 1.0 \
  --rollout-stop-token-ids 1 130073 \
  --rollout-seed "$SEED" \
  --seed "$SEED" \
  --advantage-estimator ppo \
  --gamma 1.0 \
  --lambd 1.0 \
  --gae-lambda-k 0.5 \
  --critic-value-bias-init 0.25 \
  --num-critic-only-steps "$NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS" \
  --critic-lr "$CRITIC_LR" \
  --critic-lr-warmup-iters "$NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS" \
  --normalize-advantages \
  --calculate-per-token-loss \
  --eps-clip 0.2 \
  --eps-clip-high 0.28 \
  --value-clip 0.2 \
  --kl-coef 0.0 \
  --kl-loss-coef 0.0 \
  --entropy-coef 0.0 \
  --optimizer adam \
  --lr "$LR" \
  --lr-decay-style constant \
  --weight-decay 0.01 \
  --adam-beta1 0.9 \
  --adam-beta2 0.98 \
  --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine 1 \
  --sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.30 \
  --sglang-max-running-requests 64 \
  --sglang-attention-backend flashinfer \
  --sglang-log-level warning \
  --sglang-context-length 2048 \
  --sglang-max-prefill-tokens 2048 \
  --sglang-max-total-tokens 65536 \

import asyncio
import logging
import time

import ray

from sglang.srt.constants import GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH, GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE, GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS

from miles.ray.placement_group import create_placement_groups, create_rollout_manager, create_training_models
from miles.utils.arguments import parse_args
from miles.utils.async_utils import eager_create_task
from miles.utils.logging_utils import configure_logger
from miles.utils.misc import should_run_periodic_action
from miles.utils.tracking_utils import finish_tracking, init_tracking

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _vram_phase(rollout_id: int, phase: str):
    logger.info(f"===== VRAM-Phase rollout={rollout_id} phase={phase} t={time.time():.1f} =====")


async def train(args):
    configure_logger()
    # allocate the GPUs
    pgs = create_placement_groups(args)
    init_tracking(args)

    # create the rollout manager, with sglang engines inside.
    # need to initialize rollout manager first to calculate num_rollout
    rollout_manager, num_rollout_per_epoch = create_rollout_manager(args, pgs["rollout"])

    # create the actor and critic models
    actor_model, critic_model = await create_training_models(args, pgs, rollout_manager)

    if args.offload_rollout:
        await rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote()

    # always update weight first so that sglang has the loaded weights from training.
    await actor_model.update_weights()

    if args.check_weight_update_equal:
        await rollout_manager.check_weights.remote(action="compare")

    if args.offload_rollout:
        await rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote()

    # special case for eval-only
    if args.num_rollout == 0 and args.eval_interval is not None:
        await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id=0)

    async def offload_train():
        if args.offload_train:
            if args.use_critic:
                await critic_model.offload()
                if rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps:
                    await actor_model.offload()
            else:
                await actor_model.offload()
        else:
            await actor_model.clear_memory()

    async def save(rollout_id):
        # Save the actor even during critic-only warmup. Its weights are unchanged, but
        # resume infers start_rollout_id from the actor ckpt; without one, a restart would
        # rewind to rollout 0 while the critic resumes from its old state, desyncing the two.
        await actor_model.save_model(
            rollout_id,
            force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
        )
        if args.use_critic:
            await critic_model.save_model(
                rollout_id,
                force_sync=rollout_id == args.num_rollout - 1,
            )
        if args.rollout_global_dataset:
            await rollout_manager.save.remote(rollout_id)

    consecutive_high_no_grad = 0

    # train loop.
    # note that for async training, one can change the position of the sync operation(ray.get).
    for rollout_id in range(args.start_rollout_id, args.num_rollout):
        if args.eval_interval is not None and rollout_id == 0 and not args.skip_eval_before_train:
            await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id)

        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "generate_start")
        rollout_data_ref = await rollout_manager.generate.remote(rollout_id)
        rollout_metrics = await rollout_manager.get_latest_rollout_metrics.remote()
        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "generate_end")

        no_grad = rollout_metrics.get("grpo_metrics/no_grad")
        if args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold is not None:
            if no_grad is None:
                consecutive_high_no_grad = 0
            elif no_grad > args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold:
                consecutive_high_no_grad += 1
                logger.warning(
                    "rollout %s grpo_metrics/no_grad=%.4f exceeded threshold %.4f (%s/%s)",
                    rollout_id,
                    no_grad,
                    args.stop_on_no_grad_threshold,
                    consecutive_high_no_grad,
                    args.stop_on_no_grad_patience,
                )
                if consecutive_high_no_grad >= args.stop_on_no_grad_patience:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Stopping early before actor update because no_grad stayed above threshold for %s rollouts",
                        consecutive_high_no_grad,
                    )
                    break
            else:
                consecutive_high_no_grad = 0

        if args.offload_rollout:
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "offload_rollout_start")
            offload_tags = [GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH]
            if "kv_cache" in args.offload_rollout_level:
                offload_tags.append(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_KV_CACHE)
            if "weight" in args.offload_rollout_level:
                offload_tags.append(GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_WEIGHTS)
            await rollout_manager.offload.remote(tags=offload_tags)
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "offload_rollout_end")

        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "train_start")
        if args.use_critic:
            critic_task = await eager_create_task(critic_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref))
            if rollout_id >= args.num_critic_only_steps:
                await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref)
            await critic_task
        else:
            await actor_model.train(rollout_id, rollout_data_ref)
        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "train_end")

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.save_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch, args.num_rollout):
            await save(rollout_id)

        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "offload_train_start")
        await offload_train()
        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "offload_train_end")

        if args.offload_rollout:
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "onload_weights_start")
            await rollout_manager.onload_weights.remote()
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "onload_weights_end")

        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "update_weights_start")
        await actor_model.update_weights()
        _vram_phase(rollout_id, "update_weights_end")

        if args.offload_rollout:
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "onload_kv_start")
            await rollout_manager.onload_kv.remote()
            _vram_phase(rollout_id, "onload_kv_end")

        if should_run_periodic_action(rollout_id, args.eval_interval, num_rollout_per_epoch):
            await rollout_manager.eval.remote(rollout_id)

    await rollout_manager.dispose.remote()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = parse_args()
    try:
        asyncio.run(train(args))
    finally:
        finish_tracking()

2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import ast
5	import json
6	import re
7	from fractions import Fraction
8	
9	ANSWER_RE = re.compile(r"<answer>(.*?)</answer>", flags=re.DOTALL)
10	ALLOWED_CHARS_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9+\-*/()\s]+")
11	
12	
13	def _eval_ast(node: ast.AST, used: list[int]) -> Fraction:
14	    if isinstance(node, ast.Expression):
15	        return _eval_ast(node.body, used)
16	    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and type(node.value) is int:
17	        used.append(node.value)
18	        return Fraction(node.value)
19	    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
20	        left = _eval_ast(node.left, used)
21	        right = _eval_ast(node.right, used)
22	        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
23	            return left + right
24	        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
25	            return left - right
26	        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
27	            return left * right
28	        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Div):
29	            if right == 0:
30	                raise ZeroDivisionError("division by zero")
31	            return left / right
32	        raise ValueError("unsupported binary op")
33	    raise ValueError("disallowed ast node")
34	
35	
36	def score_countdown(solution_str: str, ground_truth) -> float:
37	    if not isinstance(solution_str, str) or ground_truth is None:
38	        return 0.0
39	    if isinstance(ground_truth, str):
40	        try:
41	            gt = json.loads(ground_truth)
42	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
43	            return 0.0
44	    elif isinstance(ground_truth, dict):
45	        gt = ground_truth
46	    else:
47	        return 0.0
48	    matches = ANSWER_RE.findall(solution_str)
49	    if not matches:
50	        return 0.0
51	    expr = matches[-1].strip()
52	    expr = (
53	        expr.replace("\\times", "*")
54	        .replace("\\div", "/")
55	        .replace("\u00d7", "*")
56	        .replace("\u00f7", "/")
57	    )
58	    if "=" in expr:
59	        expr = expr.split("=")[0].strip()
60	    if not expr or len(expr) > 256 or not ALLOWED_CHARS_RE.fullmatch(expr):
61	        return 0.0
62	    try:
63	        tree = ast.parse(expr, mode="eval")
64	        used: list[int] = []
65	        val = _eval_ast(tree, used)
66	    except (SyntaxError, ZeroDivisionError, ValueError, RecursionError):
67	        return 0.0
68	    expected_nums = sorted(int(x) for x in gt["numbers"])
69	    if sorted(used) != expected_nums:
70	        return 0.0
71	    return 1.0 if val == Fraction(int(gt["target"])) else 0.0
72	
73	
74	async def compute_reward(args, sample, **kwargs) -> float:
75	    """Async custom reward entry point for Miles (--custom-rm-path)."""
76	    return float(score_countdown(getattr(sample, "response", ""), getattr(sample, "label", None)))

9

11	TEST_ROWS = 1024
12	
13	PROMPT_TEMPLATE = (
14	    "Solve the Countdown arithmetic puzzle. Using the given numbers, form an arithmetic "
15	    "expression with +, -, *, /, and parentheses that equals the target integer. "
16	    "Use each given number exactly once. Keep your reasoning brief and output only the "
17	    "final expression (without '= target') inside <answer>...</answer> tags.

"
18	    "Example 1:
"

"
20	    "Target: 21
"

"

"

"
25	    "Target: 26
"

"
27	    "<answer>8 * 2 + 6 + 4</answer>

"
28	    "Example 3:
"
29	    "Numbers: [25, 7, 4, 2]
"
30	    "Target: 43
"
31	    "Reasoning: 7 * 2 = 14, 25 + 14 = 39, and 39 + 4 = 43.
"
32	    "<answer>25 + 7 * 2 + 4</answer>

"
33	    "Now solve:
"
34	    "Numbers: {nums}
"
35	    "Target: {target}
"
36	    "Reasoning:"
37	)

42	    return {
43	        "prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
44	        "label": json.dumps({"numbers": numbers, "target": target}, sort_keys=True),
45	        "metadata": {
46	            "split": split,
47	            "index": idx,
48	            "data_source": "Jiayi-Pan/Countdown-Tasks-3to4",
49	        },
50	    }

56	        for row in rows:
57	            fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "
")

60	def from_parquet(src: Path, out: Path) -> None:
61	    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
62	
63	    parquet_path = src if src.is_file() else src / "data" / "train-00000-of-00001.parquet"
64	    table = pq.read_table(parquet_path)
65	    total = table.num_rows
66	    assert total >= TRAIN_ROWS + TEST_ROWS, f"Need >= {TRAIN_ROWS + TEST_ROWS} rows, got {total}"
67	    targets = table["target"].to_pylist()
68	    nums_list = table["nums"].to_pylist()
69	
70	    train_rows = [
71	        make_row(int(targets[i]), [int(x) for x in nums_list[i]], "train", i)
72	        for i in range(TRAIN_ROWS)
73	    ]
74	    test_start = total - TEST_ROWS
75	    test_rows = [
76	        make_row(int(targets[i]), [int(x) for x in nums_list[i]], "test", i)
77	        for i in range(test_start, total)
78	    ]
79	    write_jsonl(out / "train.jsonl", train_rows)
80	    write_jsonl(out / "test.jsonl", test_rows)
81	    print(f"train: {len(train_rows)} rows, test: {len(test_rows)} rows (disjoint from {total} total)")
82

84	def pack_binary(src_parquet: Path, out_bin: Path) -> None:
85	    """Pack exact TRAIN_ROWS + TEST_ROWS integer tuples for air-gapped cluster staging."""
86	    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
87	
88	    table = pq.read_table(src_parquet)
89	    total = table.num_rows
90	    targets = table["target"].to_pylist()
91	    nums_list = table["nums"].to_pylist()
92	    buf = bytearray()
93	    buf.extend(total.to_bytes(4, "little"))
94	    buf.extend(TRAIN_ROWS.to_bytes(4, "little"))
95	    buf.extend(TEST_ROWS.to_bytes(4, "little"))
96	    for idx in list(range(TRAIN_ROWS)) + list(range(total - TEST_ROWS, total)):
97	        ns = [int(x) for x in nums_list[idx]]
98	        buf.append(int(targets[idx]))
99	        buf.append(len(ns))
100	        for x in ns:
101	            buf.append(x)
102	    out_bin.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
103	    out_bin.write_bytes(zlib.compress(bytes(buf), 9))
104	    print(f"Packed {TRAIN_ROWS}+{TEST_ROWS} rows from {total} -> {out_bin} ({out_bin.stat().st_size} bytes)")
105

107	def unpack_binary(src_bin: Path, out: Path) -> None:
108	    raw = zlib.decompress(src_bin.read_bytes())
109	    total = int.from_bytes(raw[0:4], "little")
110	    n_train = int.from_bytes(raw[4:8], "little")
111	    n_test = int.from_bytes(raw[8:12], "little")
112	    pos = 12
113	    train_rows = []
114	    for i in range(n_train):
115	        target = raw[pos]
116	        k = raw[pos + 1]
117	        nums = list(raw[pos + 2 : pos + 2 + k])
118	        pos += 2 + k
119	        train_rows.append(make_row(target, nums, "train", i))
120	    test_start = total - n_test
121	    test_rows = []
122	    for offset in range(n_test):
123	        target = raw[pos]
124	        k = raw[pos + 1]
125	        nums = list(raw[pos + 2 : pos + 2 + k])
126	        pos += 2 + k
127	        test_rows.append(make_row(target, nums, "test", test_start + offset))
128	    assert pos == len(raw), f"trailing bytes: {pos} != {len(raw)}"
129	    write_jsonl(out / "train.jsonl", train_rows)

131	    print(f"Unpacked train: {len(train_rows)} rows, test: {len(test_rows)} rows (total={total})")

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import zlib
from pathlib import Path

TRAIN_ROWS = 8192
TEST_ROWS = 1024

PROMPT_TEMPLATE = (
    "Solve the Countdown arithmetic puzzle. Using the given numbers, form an arithmetic "
    "expression with +, -, *, /, and parentheses that equals the target integer. "
    "Use each given number exactly once. Keep your reasoning brief and output only the "
    "final expression (without '= target') inside <answer>...</answer> tags.\n\n"
    "Example 1:\n"
    "Numbers: [12, 3, 5]\n"
    "Target: 21\n"
    "Reasoning: 12 - 5 = 7, and 3 * 7 = 21.\n"
    "<answer>3 * (12 - 5)</answer>\n\n"
    "Example 2:\n"
    "Numbers: [8, 4, 2, 6]\n"
    "Target: 26\n"
    "Reasoning: 8 * 2 = 16, and 16 + 6 + 4 = 26.\n"
    "<answer>8 * 2 + 6 + 4</answer>\n\n"
    "Example 3:\n"
    "Numbers: [25, 7, 4, 2]\n"
    "Target: 43\n"
    "Reasoning: 7 * 2 = 14, 25 + 14 = 39, and 39 + 4 = 43.\n"
    "<answer>25 + 7 * 2 + 4</answer>\n\n"
    "Now solve:\n"
    "Numbers: {nums}\n"
    "Target: {target}\n"
    "Reasoning:"
)


def make_row(target: int, numbers: list[int], split: str, idx: int) -> dict:
    content = PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(nums=numbers, target=target)
    return {
        "prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
        "label": json.dumps({"numbers": numbers, "target": target}, sort_keys=True),
        "metadata": {
            "split": split,
            "index": idx,
            "data_source": "Jiayi-Pan/Countdown-Tasks-3to4",
        },
    }


def write_jsonl(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for row in rows:
            fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


def from_parquet(src: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    parquet_path = src if src.is_file() else src / "data" / "train-00000-of-00001.parquet"
    table = pq.read_table(parquet_path)
    total = table.num_rows
    assert total >= TRAIN_ROWS + TEST_ROWS, f"Need >= {TRAIN_ROWS + TEST_ROWS} rows, got {total}"
    targets = table["target"].to_pylist()
    nums_list = table["nums"].to_pylist()

    train_rows = [
        make_row(int(targets[i]), [int(x) for x in nums_list[i]], "train", i)
        for i in range(TRAIN_ROWS)
    ]
    test_start = total - TEST_ROWS
    test_rows = [
        make_row(int(targets[i]), [int(x) for x in nums_list[i]], "test", i)
        for i in range(test_start, total)
    ]

    write_jsonl(out / "test.jsonl", test_rows)

    buf.extend(TEST_ROWS.to_bytes(4, "little"))

        for x in ns:
            buf.append(x)
    out_bin.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_bin.write_bytes(zlib.compress(bytes(buf), 9))
    print(f"Packed {TRAIN_ROWS}+{TEST_ROWS} rows from {total} -> {out_bin} ({out_bin.stat().st_size} bytes)")


def unpack_binary(src_bin: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    raw = zlib.decompress(src_bin.read_bytes())
    total = int.from_bytes(raw[0:4], "little")
    n_train = int.from_bytes(raw[4:8], "little")
    n_test = int.from_bytes(raw[8:12], "little")

        target = raw[pos]
        k = raw[pos + 1]

    write_jsonl(out / "test.jsonl", test_rows)
    print(f"Unpacked train: {len(train_rows)} rows, test: {len(test_rows)} rows (total={total})")


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--src", type=Path, help="Countdown snapshot dir or parquet file")
    ap.add_argument("--src-bin", type=Path, help="Packed binary countdown file")
    ap.add_argument("--pack-to", type=Path, help="Pack parquet to compact binary")

rows = []

def compute_advantages_and_returns(args: Namespace, rollout_data: RolloutBatch) -> None:
    """Compute advantages and returns in-place based on `args.advantage_estimator`.

    This function extracts rewards, log-probs, values, and masks from
    `rollout_data`, computes KL divergences, then applies the chosen advantage
    estimator. Supported methods: "grpo", "gspo", "ppo", "reinforce_plus_plus",
    and "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline". When `args.normalize_advantages` is
    True, advantages are whitened across the data-parallel group using masked
    statistics.

    Early returns if both `log_probs` and `values` are None (intermediate
    pipeline stages).

    Args:
        args: Configuration specifying estimator type, KL coefficient,
            normalization settings, and other hyperparameters.
        rollout_data: Dict containing input lists ("log_probs", "ref_log_probs",
            "rewards", "values", "response_lengths", "loss_masks",
            "total_lengths"). Modified in-place to add "advantages" and
            "returns" keys, each mapping to lists of tensors per sample.
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()

            for i in range(len(advantages)):
                total_len = total_lengths[i]
                response_len = response_lengths[i]
                prompt_len = total_len - response_len
                max_seq_len = max_seq_lens[i] if max_seq_lens is not None else None

                _, _, _, token_offsets = get_logits_and_tokens_offset_with_cp(
                    total_len, response_len, args.qkv_format, max_seq_len
                )

                # Convert global offsets to response-space offsets
                s0, e0 = token_offsets[0]
                s1, e1 = token_offsets[1]
                res_s0, res_e0 = max(0, s0 - prompt_len), max(0, e0 - prompt_len)
                res_s1, res_e1 = max(0, s1 - prompt_len), max(0, e1 - prompt_len)

                local_mask_parts = []
                full_mask = loss_masks[i]
                if res_e0 > res_s0:
                    local_mask_parts.append(full_mask[res_s0:res_e0])
                if res_e1 > res_s1:
                    local_mask_parts.append(full_mask[res_s1:res_e1])

                # Concatenate the parts to form the final mask chunk for this rank and this sequence
                local_mask_chunk = (
                    torch.cat(local_mask_parts)
                    if local_mask_parts
                    else torch.tensor([], device=all_advs.device, dtype=full_mask.dtype)
                )
                mask_chunks.append(local_mask_chunk)

            all_masks = torch.cat(mask_chunks)

        assert (
            all_advs.size() == all_masks.size()
        ), f"Shape mismatch before whitening: advantages {all_advs.size()}, masks {all_masks.size()}"
        dp_group = parallel_state.intra_dp.group

        group_size = max(1, int(getattr(args, "n_samples_per_prompt", 1)))
        if len(advantages) >= group_size and len(advantages) % group_size == 0:
            whitened_chunks = []
            mask_list = (
                list(loss_masks)
                if cp_size == 1
                else list(torch.split(all_masks, [chunk.size(0) for chunk in advantages]))
            )
            for g_start in range(0, len(advantages), group_size):
                g_advs = advantages[g_start : g_start + group_size]
                g_masks = mask_list[g_start : g_start + group_size]
                g_adv_flat = torch.cat(g_advs)
                g_mask_flat = torch.cat(g_masks)
                g_whitened = distributed_masked_whiten(
                    g_adv_flat,
                    g_mask_flat,
                    process_group=dp_group,
                    shift_mean=True,
                )
                whitened_chunks.extend(torch.split(g_whitened, [c.size(0) for c in g_advs]))
            advantages = whitened_chunks
        else:
            whitened_advs_flat = distributed_masked_whiten(
                all_advs,
                all_masks,
                process_group=dp_group,
                shift_mean=True,
            )
            chunk_lengths = [chunk.size(0) for chunk in advantages]
            advantages = list(torch.split(whitened_advs_flat, chunk_lengths))

    rollout_data["advantages"] = advantages
    rollout_data["returns"] = returns


def vanilla_tis_function(
    args,
    *,
    pg_loss: torch.Tensor,
    train_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    rollout_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor],
    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor],
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, list[torch.Tensor], dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    rollout_log_probs = torch.cat(rollout_log_probs, dim=0)
    old_log_probs = torch.cat(train_log_probs, dim=0)
    tis = torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs)
    tis_abs = (torch.exp(old_log_probs - rollout_log_probs) - 1).abs()
    tis_weights = torch.clamp(tis, min=args.tis_clip_low, max=args.tis_clip)
    tis_clipfrac = (tis_weights != tis).float()
    metrics = {
        "tis": tis.clone().detach(),
        "tis_clipfrac": tis_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
        "tis_abs": tis_abs.clone().detach(),
    }
    pg_loss = pg_loss * tis_weights
    return pg_loss, loss_masks, metrics

    pipeline stages).

            normalization settings, and other hyperparameters.

            "returns" keys, each mapping to lists of tensors per sample.
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()
    log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("rollout_log_probs" if args.use_rollout_logprobs else "log_probs")
    ref_log_probs: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("ref_log_probs")
    rewards: list[float] = rollout_data.get("rewards")
    values: None | list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("values")
    response_lengths: list[int] = rollout_data.get("response_lengths")
    loss_masks: list[torch.Tensor] = rollout_data.get("loss_masks")

    max_seq_lens: list[int] | None = rollout_data.get("max_seq_lens", None)

    if log_probs is None and values is None:

    if args.kl_coef == 0 or not log_probs:
        # when kl_coef is 0, we won't compute ref_log_prob
        xs = log_probs if log_probs is not None else values
        kl = [torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device) for x in xs]
    else:
        kl = [
            compute_approx_kl(
                log_probs[i],
                ref_log_probs[i],

            )

            kl_coef=args.kl_coef,
        )
        returns = advantages

        response_lengths = rollout_data.get("response_lengths")

1427	def value_loss_function(
1428	    args: Namespace,
1429	    batch: RolloutBatch,
1430	    logits: torch.Tensor,
1431	    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
1432	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
1433	    """Compute clipped value loss and metrics.
1434	
1435	    Extracts current value predictions from `logits`, compares them against
1436	    stored old values with clipping, and computes the maximum of clipped and
1437	    unclipped squared errors (PPO-style value clipping).
1438	
1439	    Args:
1440	        args: Configuration containing `value_clip` threshold.
1441	        batch: Mini-batch with "values" (old predictions), "returns",
1442	            "unconcat_tokens", "total_lengths", and "response_lengths".
1443	        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
1444	        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.
1445	
1446	    Returns:
1447	        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `loss` is a scalar tensor and
1448	        `metrics` contains detached scalars "value_loss" and "value_clipfrac".
1449	    """
1450	    old_values = torch.cat(batch["values"], dim=0)
1451	
1452	    values = get_values(
1453	        logits,
1454	        args=args,
1455	        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
1456	        total_lengths=batch["total_lengths"],
1457	        response_lengths=batch["response_lengths"],
1458	        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
1459	    )
1460	    values = torch.cat([value.flatten() for value in values["values"]], dim=0)
1461	
1462	    returns = torch.cat(batch["returns"], dim=0)
1463	
1464	    values_clipfrac = torch.abs(values - old_values) > args.value_clip
1465	    values_clipped = old_values + (values - old_values).clamp(-args.value_clip, args.value_clip)
1466	    surr1 = (values_clipped - returns) ** 2
1467	    surr2 = (values - returns) ** 2
1468	    loss = torch.max(surr1, surr2)
1469	
1470	    loss = sum_of_sample_mean(loss)
1471	    values_clipfrac = sum_of_sample_mean(values_clipfrac.float())
1472	
1473	    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
1474	    if values.numel() == 0:
1475	        loss += 0 * values.sum()
1476	
1477	    reported_loss = {
1478	        "value_loss": loss.clone().detach(),
1479	        "value_clipfrac": values_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
1480	    }
1481	
1482	    return loss, reported_loss

1485	def sft_loss_function(
1486	    args: Namespace,
1487	    batch: RolloutBatch,
1488	    logits: torch.Tensor,
1489	    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
1490	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
1491	    """Compute supervised fine-tuning loss over response tokens.
1492	
1493	    Computes log-probabilities of the ground-truth tokens in the response
1494	    segments and returns the negative log-likelihood as the loss.
1495	
1496	    Args:
1497	        args: Configuration (passed through to helpers).
1498	        batch: Mini-batch with "unconcat_tokens", "response_lengths", and
1499	            "total_lengths".
1500	        logits: Policy logits with shape `[1, T, V]`.
1501	        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.
1502	
1503	    Returns:
1504	        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `metrics` contains a single detached
1505	        scalar "loss".
1506	    """
1507	    response_lengths = batch["response_lengths"]
1508	    total_lengths = batch["total_lengths"]
1509	
1510	    _chunked_logits_params = batch.get("_chunked_logits_params")
1511	    log_probs_and_entropy = get_log_probs_and_entropy(
1512	        logits,
1513	        args=args,
1514	        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
1515	        total_lengths=total_lengths,
1516	        response_lengths=response_lengths,
1517	        with_entropy=False,
1518	        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
1519	        _chunked_logits_params=_chunked_logits_params,
1520	    )
1521	
1522	    log_probs = log_probs_and_entropy["log_probs"]

1527	    if log_probs.numel() == 0:
1528	        loss += 0 * logits.sum()
1529	
1530	    return (
1531	        loss,
1532	        {
1533	            "loss": loss.clone().detach(),
1534	        },
1535	    )

1538	def loss_function(
1539	    args: Namespace,
1540	    batch: RolloutBatch,
1541	    num_microbatches: int,
1542	    logits: torch.Tensor,
1543	    apply_megatron_loss_scaling: bool = False,

1568	    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()

1570	    num_samples = len(batch["response_lengths"])
1571	
1572	    sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(
1573	        batch["total_lengths"],
1574	        batch["response_lengths"],
1575	        batch["loss_masks"],
1576	        args.calculate_per_token_loss,
1577	        args.qkv_format,
1578	        batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
1579	    )
1580	
1581	    match args.loss_type:
1582	        case "policy_loss":
1583	            func = policy_loss_function
1584	        case "value_loss":
1585	            func = value_loss_function
1586	        case "sft_loss":
1587	            func = sft_loss_function
1588	        case "custom_loss":
1589	            func = load_function(args.custom_loss_function_path)

1592	
1593	    if args.recompute_loss_function:
1594	        loss, log = checkpoint(
1595	            func,
1596	            args,
1597	            batch,
1598	            logits,
1599	            sum_of_sample_mean,
1600	            use_reentrant=True,
1601	        )
1602	    else:
1603	        loss, log = func(args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean)
1604	
1605	    # With allgather-CP, some CP ranks may have no loss-contributing tokens (e.g., all

1607	    # the CP gather's backward (reduce-scatter) is not called, deadlocking other CP
1608	    # ranks that call it. Adding this zero loss forces autograd to traverse the full
1609	    # graph on every rank without changing gradient values.
1610	    if parallel_state.cp.size > 1 and args.allgather_cp:

1615	    global_batch_size = batch.get("dynamic_global_batch_size", args.global_batch_size)
1616	    if not args.calculate_per_token_loss:
1617	        if apply_megatron_loss_scaling:
1618	            loss_parallel_size = (
1619	                parallel_state.intra_dp.size
1620	                if args.true_on_policy_mode and parallel_state.is_ulysses_cp
1621	                else parallel_state.intra_dp_cp.size
1622	            )
1623	            loss = loss * num_microbatches / global_batch_size * loss_parallel_size
1624	        else:
1625	            loss = loss / global_batch_size * parallel_state.intra_dp.size
1626	    else:
1627	        if apply_megatron_loss_scaling:
1628	            loss = loss * parallel_state.cp.size
1629	
1630	    weighted_metrics = {
1631	        key.removeprefix("_weighted/"): value.detach()
1632	        for key, value in log.items()
1633	        if key.startswith("_weighted/")
1634	    }
1635	    metric_items = [

1637	        for key, value in log.items()
1638	        if not key.startswith("_") and not key.startswith("_weighted/")
1639	    ]
1640	    logging_dict = {

1642	        "values": torch.tensor(
1643	            [
1644	                num_samples if not args.calculate_per_token_loss else num_tokens,
1645	            ]
1646	            + [value for _, value in metric_items],

1649	    }

1655	        logging_dict["logdiff_min_max"] = log["_logdiff_min_max"].detach()
1656	
1657	    return (
1658	        loss,
1659	        torch.tensor(num_tokens if args.calculate_per_token_loss else 1, device=logits.device),
1660	        logging_dict,
1661	    )

def policy_loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Compute policy loss (PPO/GSPO) and metrics.

    Computes current log-probabilities and entropy from model logits, then
    calculates PPO-style clipped policy gradient loss. For GSPO, gathers
    full sequences via context-parallel all-gather before computing per-sample
    KL. Optionally applies TIS (Truncated Importance Sampling) correction and
    adds KL loss term if configured.

    Args:
        args: Configuration controlling advantage estimator, clipping thresholds,
            entropy/KL coefficients, and TIS settings.
        batch: Mini-batch containing "advantages", "log_probs" (old policy),
            "unconcat_tokens", "response_lengths", "total_lengths", "loss_masks",
            and optionally "ref_log_probs" and "rollout_log_probs".
        logits: Policy logits with shape `[1, T, V]`.
        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `loss` is a scalar tensor and `metrics`
        is a dict containing detached scalars: "loss", "pg_loss",
        "entropy_loss", "pg_clipfrac", "ppo_kl". Additional keys "kl_loss",
        "tis", "ois", "tis_clipfrac" are included when the respective features
        are enabled.
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()
    advantages = torch.cat(batch["advantages"], dim=0)
    old_log_probs = batch["rollout_log_probs"] if args.use_rollout_logprobs else batch["log_probs"]

    response_lengths = batch["response_lengths"]
    total_lengths = batch["total_lengths"]
    max_seq_lens = batch.get("max_seq_lens", None)

    _need_entropy = args.entropy_coef != 0
    _chunked_logits_params = batch.get("_chunked_logits_params")
    log_probs_and_entropy = get_log_probs_and_entropy(
        logits,
        args=args,
        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
        total_lengths=total_lengths,
        response_lengths=response_lengths,
        with_entropy=_need_entropy,
        max_seq_lens=max_seq_lens,
        _chunked_logits_params=_chunked_logits_params,
    )

    log_probs = log_probs_and_entropy["log_probs"]
    train_log_probs_list = log_probs
    old_log_probs_list = old_log_probs

    # Pre-gather log probs if needed by OPSM or GSPO to avoid duplicate gathering
    need_full_log_probs = args.use_opsm or args.advantage_estimator == "gspo"

    full_log_probs = None
    full_old_log_probs = None
    if need_full_log_probs:
        full_log_probs = [
            all_gather_with_cp(log_prob, total_length, response_length)
            for log_prob, total_length, response_length in zip(
                log_probs, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
            )
        ]
        full_old_log_probs = [
            all_gather_with_cp(old_log_prob, total_length, response_length)
            for old_log_prob, total_length, response_length in zip(
                old_log_probs, total_lengths, response_lengths, strict=False
            )
        ]

    # Compute OPSM mask if enabled
    if args.use_opsm:
        opsm_mask, opsm_clipfrac = compute_opsm_mask(
            args=args,
            full_log_probs=full_log_probs,
            full_old_log_probs=full_old_log_probs,
            advantages=batch["advantages"],
            loss_masks=batch["loss_masks"],
        )

    # Compute KL divergence (GSPO uses sequence-level KL, others use per-token KL)
    if args.advantage_estimator == "gspo":
        ppo_kl = compute_gspo_kl(
            full_log_probs=full_log_probs,
            full_old_log_probs=full_old_log_probs,
            local_log_probs=log_probs,
            loss_masks=batch["loss_masks"],
        )
        old_log_probs = torch.cat(old_log_probs, dim=0)
        log_probs = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0)
    else:
        old_log_probs = torch.cat(old_log_probs, dim=0)
        log_probs = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0)
        ppo_kl = old_log_probs - log_probs

    local_loss_mask_list = get_local_response_loss_masks(
        total_lengths,
        response_lengths,
        batch["loss_masks"],
        args.qkv_format,
        max_seq_lens,
    )
    local_loss_masks = torch.cat(local_loss_mask_list, dim=0).to(device=ppo_kl.device)
    active_tokens = local_loss_masks.bool()
    ppo_kl = torch.where(
        active_tokens,
        torch.nan_to_num(ppo_kl, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0),
        ppo_kl.new_zeros(()),
    )
    advantages = torch.where(
        active_tokens,
        torch.nan_to_num(advantages, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0),
        advantages.new_zeros(()),
    )

    pg_loss, pg_clipfrac = compute_policy_loss(ppo_kl, advantages, args.eps_clip, args.eps_clip_high)

    if getattr(args, "dump_details", None) is not None:
        from .debug_dump import maybe_dump_policy_loss_debug

        maybe_dump_policy_loss_debug(
            args=args,
            batch=batch,
            train_log_probs=train_log_probs_list,
            old_log_probs=old_log_probs_list,
            rollout_log_probs=batch.get("rollout_log_probs"),
            advantages=batch["advantages"],
            local_loss_masks=local_loss_mask_list,
            ppo_kl=ppo_kl,
            pg_loss=pg_loss,
        )

    if args.use_opsm:
        pg_loss = pg_loss * opsm_mask

    # Apply off-policy correction using importance sampling if enabled
    if args.get_mismatch_metrics or args.use_tis:
        # NOTE:
        # `tis_func` may apply rejection-sampling style masking (RS) and return `modified_response_masks`.
        # We rebuild `sum_of_sample_mean` with those masks to correct denominators for loss/backprop.
        #
        # However, mismatch/TIS/RS metrics (e.g., "truncate_fraction") are often defined over the
        # *pre-RS* valid tokens. If we aggregate metrics with `modified_response_masks`, the rejected
        # tokens are excluded from the denominator and the metric can be artificially driven to 0.
        # Keep a copy of the original reducer (based on `batch["loss_masks"]`) for metric aggregation.
        sum_of_sample_mean_for_mismatch_metrics = sum_of_sample_mean

        assert "rollout_log_probs" in batch, "rollout_log_probs must be provided for TIS"

        ois = (-ppo_kl).exp()
        tis_kwargs = {
            "args": args,
            "pg_loss": pg_loss,
            "train_log_probs": batch["log_probs"],
            "rollout_log_probs": batch["rollout_log_probs"],
            "loss_masks": batch["loss_masks"],
            "total_lengths": total_lengths,
            "response_lengths": response_lengths,
            "parallel_state": parallel_state,
            "max_seq_lens": max_seq_lens,
        }

        if args.custom_tis_function_path is not None:

        sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(

    else:

    ess_ratio_sum, ess_ratio_weight = compute_ess_ratio_contribution(
        ppo_kl=ppo_kl,

    # entropy loss (skip expensive computation when entropy_coef == 0)

    loss = pg_loss - args.entropy_coef * entropy_loss

    if args.use_kl_loss:
        ref_log_probs = batch["ref_log_probs"]
        ref_log_probs = torch.cat(ref_log_probs, dim=0)
        importance_ratio = None
        if args.use_unbiased_kl:

        kl = compute_approx_kl(
            log_probs,
            ref_log_probs,

        kl = torch.where(
            active_tokens,

        kl_loss = sum_of_sample_mean(kl)

        if args.kl_loss_coef != 0:

    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
    if log_probs.numel() == 0:

    disable_logdiff_metrics = os.environ.get("MILES_DISABLE_LOGDIFF_METRICS", "0").lower() in {"1", "true", "yes"}

    train_scored_log_probs = log_probs
    train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff = None
    train_rollout_kl = None
    if not disable_logdiff_metrics and "rollout_log_probs" in batch and batch["rollout_log_probs"]:

            from miles.utils.debug_utils.icepop_dump import record_icepop_scatter

            # Use ``old_log_probs`` (== batch["log_probs"], the same tensor IcePop/TIS
            # feeds into its ratio) so the offline keep/mask decision matches training.
            record_icepop_scatter(
                args,

            )

        abs_diff_raw = (train_scored_log_probs - rollout_log_probs).abs()
        abs_diff = torch.where(
            active_tokens,

        rollout_train_kl = torch.where(
            active_tokens,
            torch.nan_to_num(rollout_train_kl, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0),
            rollout_train_kl.new_zeros(()),

        "pg_loss": pg_loss.clone().detach(),
        "entropy_loss": entropy_loss.clone().detach(),

        "ppo_kl": ppo_kl.clone().detach(),

    if ess_ratio_weight is None:
        reported_loss["ess_ratio"] = ess_ratio_sum.squeeze()
    else:
        reported_loss["_weighted/ess_ratio"] = torch.stack([ess_ratio_sum.squeeze(), ess_ratio_weight.squeeze()])

        reported_loss["train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff"] = train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff.clone().detach()
    if train_rollout_kl is not None:
        reported_loss["train_rollout_kl"] = train_rollout_kl.clone().detach()

        with torch.no_grad():
            metric_diff = torch.where(
                active_tokens,
                torch.nan_to_num(abs_diff_raw, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0),
                abs_diff_raw.new_zeros(()),
            )

            if args.calculate_per_token_loss:
                if flat_diff.numel() > 0:
                    reported_loss["_logdiff_histogram"] = _make_logdiff_histogram(flat_diff)
                    reported_loss["_logdiff_min_max"] = torch.stack([flat_diff.min(), flat_diff.max()]).to(
                        dtype=torch.float64
                    )
                else:
                    reported_loss["_logdiff_histogram"] = torch.zeros(
                        _LOGDIFF_HISTOGRAM_BINS + 1, device=flat_diff.device, dtype=torch.float64
                    )
                    reported_loss["_logdiff_min_max"] = torch.tensor(
                        [float("inf"), float("-inf")], device=flat_diff.device, dtype=torch.float64
                    )
            elif flat_diff.numel() > 0:
                sorted_diff = flat_diff.sort().values
                n = sorted_diff.numel()
                for tag, q in [("p50", 0.5), ("p75", 0.75), ("p90", 0.9), ("p95", 0.95), ("p999", 0.999)]:
                    idx = min(int(q * n), n - 1)
                    reported_loss[f"logdiff_{tag}"] = sorted_diff[idx]
                reported_loss["logdiff_min"] = sorted_diff[0]
                reported_loss["logdiff_max"] = sorted_diff[-1]

            ref_list = batch["rollout_log_probs"]
            offset = 0
            per_sample_max_list = []
            for sample_lp, sample_mask in zip(ref_list, local_loss_mask_list, strict=True):
                seg_len = sample_lp.size(0)
                sample_mask = sample_mask.to(device=metric_diff.device, dtype=torch.bool)
                sample_diff = metric_diff[offset : offset + seg_len]
                if sample_mask.any():
                    per_sample_max_list.append(sample_diff[sample_mask].max())
                elif args.calculate_per_token_loss:
                    per_sample_max_list.append(flat_diff.new_full((), float("-inf")))
                offset += seg_len
            if per_sample_max_list:
                per_sample_max = torch.stack(per_sample_max_list)

                    if parallel_state.cp.size > 1:
                        dist.all_reduce(per_sample_max, op=dist.ReduceOp.MAX, group=parallel_state.cp.group)
                    finite_sample_max = per_sample_max[torch.isfinite(per_sample_max)]
                    numerator = finite_sample_max.sum() if finite_sample_max.numel() > 0 else flat_diff.new_zeros(())

                    if parallel_state.cp.size > 1 and parallel_state.cp.rank != 0:
                        numerator = numerator * 0
                        denominator = denominator * 0
                    reported_loss["_weighted/logdiff_token_max_per_sample"] = torch.stack(
                        [numerator.squeeze(), denominator.squeeze()]
                    )
                else:
                    reported_loss["logdiff_token_max_per_sample"] = per_sample_max.mean()

            if flat_diff.numel() > 0:
                _accumulate_logdiff_histogram(flat_diff)
                if metric_diff.max().item() > 0.5:
                    _log_extreme_logdiff_diagnostic(
                        flat_diff=metric_diff.detach().float(),

        # See comment above where `sum_of_sample_mean_for_mismatch_metrics` is defined.

    return loss, reported_loss


def value_loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Compute clipped value loss and metrics.

    Extracts current value predictions from `logits`, compares them against
    stored old values with clipping, and computes the maximum of clipped and
    unclipped squared errors (PPO-style value clipping).

    Args:
        args: Configuration containing `value_clip` threshold.
        batch: Mini-batch with "values" (old predictions), "returns",
            "unconcat_tokens", "total_lengths", and "response_lengths".
        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `loss` is a scalar tensor and
        `metrics` contains detached scalars "value_loss" and "value_clipfrac".
    """
    old_values = torch.cat(batch["values"], dim=0)

    values = get_values(
        logits,
        args=args,
        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
        total_lengths=batch["total_lengths"],
        response_lengths=batch["response_lengths"],
        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
    )
    values = torch.cat([value.flatten() for value in values["values"]], dim=0)

    returns = torch.cat(batch["returns"], dim=0)

    values_clipfrac = torch.abs(values - old_values) > args.value_clip
    values_clipped = old_values + (values - old_values).clamp(-args.value_clip, args.value_clip)
    surr1 = (values_clipped - returns) ** 2
    surr2 = (values - returns) ** 2
    loss = torch.max(surr1, surr2)

    loss = sum_of_sample_mean(loss)
    values_clipfrac = sum_of_sample_mean(values_clipfrac.float())

    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
    if values.numel() == 0:
        loss += 0 * values.sum()

    reported_loss = {
        "value_loss": loss.clone().detach(),
        "value_clipfrac": values_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
    }

    return loss, reported_loss


def sft_loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Compute supervised fine-tuning loss over response tokens.

    Computes log-probabilities of the ground-truth tokens in the response
    segments and returns the negative log-likelihood as the loss.

    Args:
        args: Configuration (passed through to helpers).
        batch: Mini-batch with "unconcat_tokens", "response_lengths", and
            "total_lengths".
        logits: Policy logits with shape `[1, T, V]`.
        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `metrics` contains a single detached
        scalar "loss".
    """
    response_lengths = batch["response_lengths"]
    total_lengths = batch["total_lengths"]

    _chunked_logits_params = batch.get("_chunked_logits_params")
    log_probs_and_entropy = get_log_probs_and_entropy(
        logits,
        args=args,
        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
        total_lengths=total_lengths,
        response_lengths=response_lengths,
        with_entropy=False,
        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
        _chunked_logits_params=_chunked_logits_params,
    )

    log_probs = log_probs_and_entropy["log_probs"]
    log_probs = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0)
    loss = -sum_of_sample_mean(log_probs)

    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
    if log_probs.numel() == 0:
        loss += 0 * logits.sum()

    return (
        loss,
        {
            "loss": loss.clone().detach(),
        },
    )


def loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    num_microbatches: int,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    apply_megatron_loss_scaling: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, int | torch.Tensor, dict[str, list[str] | torch.Tensor]]:
    """Dispatch to the configured loss and rescale for Megatron integration.

    Selects one of "policy_loss", "value_loss", "sft_loss", or a custom loss
    function based on `args.loss_type`, computes the loss and metrics, then
    rescales the loss by micro-batch and parallelism factors to integrate with
    Megatron's gradient accumulation.

    Args:
        args: Configuration specifying `loss_type`, `calculate_per_token_loss`,
            `global_batch_size`, and optionally `custom_loss_function_path`.
        batch: Mini-batch with "loss_masks", "response_lengths", and other
            keys required by the selected loss function.
        num_microbatches: Number of gradient accumulation steps.
        logits: Model outputs (policy or value head).

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(scaled_loss, normalizer, logging_dict)` where:
        - `scaled_loss` is the loss tensor (scalar) rescaled for Megatron.
        - `normalizer` is `num_tokens` (scalar tensor) if
          `args.calculate_per_token_loss` is True, else `1` (int).
        - `logging_dict` has keys "keys" (list of str metric names) and
          "values" (1D tensor: [count, metric1, metric2, ...]).
    """
    parallel_state = get_parallel_state()
    num_tokens = sum([torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1) for loss_mask in batch["loss_masks"]])
    num_samples = len(batch["response_lengths"])

    sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(
        batch["total_lengths"],
        batch["response_lengths"],
        batch["loss_masks"],
        args.calculate_per_token_loss,
        args.qkv_format,
        batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
    )

    match args.loss_type:
        case "policy_loss":
            func = policy_loss_function
        case "value_loss":
            func = value_loss_function
        case "sft_loss":
            func = sft_loss_function
        case "custom_loss":
            func = load_function(args.custom_loss_function_path)
        case _:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {args.loss_type}")

    if args.recompute_loss_function:
        loss, log = checkpoint(
            func,
            args,
            batch,
            logits,
            sum_of_sample_mean,
            use_reentrant=True,
        )
    else:
        loss, log = func(args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean)

    # With allgather-CP, some CP ranks may have no loss-contributing tokens (e.g., all
    # padding). Without this, gradient doesn't flow through their attention path, so
    # the CP gather's backward (reduce-scatter) is not called, deadlocking other CP
    # ranks that call it. Adding this zero loss forces autograd to traverse the full
    # graph on every rank without changing gradient values.
    if parallel_state.cp.size > 1 and args.allgather_cp:
        loss = loss + 0 * logits.sum()

    # Here we need to divide by cp_size because to cancel the multiply in Megatron.
    assert args.use_dynamic_global_batch_size == ("dynamic_global_batch_size" in batch)
    global_batch_size = batch.get("dynamic_global_batch_size", args.global_batch_size)
    if not args.calculate_per_token_loss:
        if apply_megatron_loss_scaling:
            loss_parallel_size = (
                parallel_state.intra_dp.size
                if args.true_on_policy_mode and parallel_state.is_ulysses_cp
                else parallel_state.intra_dp_cp.size
            )
            loss = loss * num_microbatches / global_batch_size * loss_parallel_size
        else:
            loss = loss / global_batch_size * parallel_state.intra_dp.size
    else:
        if apply_megatron_loss_scaling:
            loss = loss * parallel_state.cp.size

    weighted_metrics = {
        key.removeprefix("_weighted/"): value.detach()
        for key, value in log.items()
        if key.startswith("_weighted/")
    }
    metric_items = [
        (key, value)
        for key, value in log.items()
        if not key.startswith("_") and not key.startswith("_weighted/")
    ]
    logging_dict = {
        "keys": [key for key, _ in metric_items],
        "values": torch.tensor(
            [
                num_samples if not args.calculate_per_token_loss else num_tokens,
            ]
            + [value for _, value in metric_items],
            device=logits.device,
        ),
    }
    if weighted_metrics:
        logging_dict["weighted_metrics"] = weighted_metrics
    if "_logdiff_histogram" in log:
        logging_dict["logdiff_histogram"] = log["_logdiff_histogram"].detach()
    if "_logdiff_min_max" in log:
        logging_dict["logdiff_min_max"] = log["_logdiff_min_max"].detach()

    return (
        loss,
        torch.tensor(num_tokens if args.calculate_per_token_loss else 1, device=logits.device),
        logging_dict,
    )

1427	def value_loss_function(
1428	    args: Namespace,
1429	    batch: RolloutBatch,
1430	    logits: torch.Tensor,
1431	    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
1432	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
1433	    """Compute clipped value loss and metrics.
1434	
1435	    Extracts current value predictions from `logits`, compares them against
1436	    stored old values with clipping, and computes the maximum of clipped and
1437	    unclipped squared errors (PPO-style value clipping).
1438	
1439	    Args:
1440	        args: Configuration containing `value_clip` threshold.
1441	        batch: Mini-batch with "values" (old predictions), "returns",
1442	            "unconcat_tokens", "total_lengths", and "response_lengths".
1443	        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
1444	        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.
1445	
1446	    Returns:
1447	        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `loss` is a scalar tensor and
1448	        `metrics` contains detached scalars "value_loss" and "value_clipfrac".
1449	    """
1450	    old_values = torch.cat(batch["values"], dim=0)
1451	
1452	    values = get_values(
1453	        logits,
1454	        args=args,
1455	        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
1456	        total_lengths=batch["total_lengths"],
1457	        response_lengths=batch["response_lengths"],
1458	        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
1459	    )
1460	    values = torch.cat([value.flatten() for value in values["values"]], dim=0)
1461	
1462	    returns = torch.cat(batch["returns"], dim=0)
1463	
1464	    values_clipfrac = torch.abs(values - old_values) > args.value_clip
1465	    values_clipped = old_values + (values - old_values).clamp(-args.value_clip, args.value_clip)
1466	    surr1 = (values_clipped - returns) ** 2
1467	    surr2 = (values - returns) ** 2
1468	    loss = torch.max(surr1, surr2)
1469	
1470	    loss = sum_of_sample_mean(loss)
1471	    values_clipfrac = sum_of_sample_mean(values_clipfrac.float())
1472	
1473	    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
1474	    if values.numel() == 0:
1475	        loss += 0 * values.sum()
1476	
1477	    reported_loss = {
1478	        "value_loss": loss.clone().detach(),
1479	        "value_clipfrac": values_clipfrac.clone().detach(),
1480	    }
1481	
1482	    return loss, reported_loss

1485	def sft_loss_function(
1486	    args: Namespace,
1487	    batch: RolloutBatch,
1488	    logits: torch.Tensor,
1489	    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
1490	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
1491	    """Compute supervised fine-tuning loss over response tokens.
1492	
1493	    Computes log-probabilities of the ground-truth tokens in the response
1494	    segments and returns the negative log-likelihood as the loss.
1495	
1496	    Args:
1497	        args: Configuration (passed through to helpers).
1498	        batch: Mini-batch with "unconcat_tokens", "response_lengths", and
1499	            "total_lengths".
1500	        logits: Policy logits with shape `[1, T, V]`.
1501	        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.
1502	
1503	    Returns:
1504	        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `metrics` contains a single detached
1505	        scalar "loss".
1506	    """
1507	    response_lengths = batch["response_lengths"]
1508	    total_lengths = batch["total_lengths"]
1509	
1510	    _chunked_logits_params = batch.get("_chunked_logits_params")
1511	    log_probs_and_entropy = get_log_probs_and_entropy(
1512	        logits,
1513	        args=args,
1514	        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
1515	        total_lengths=total_lengths,
1516	        response_lengths=response_lengths,
1517	        with_entropy=False,
1518	        max_seq_lens=batch.get("max_seq_lens", None),
1519	        _chunked_logits_params=_chunked_logits_params,
1520	    )
1521	
1522	    log_probs = log_probs_and_entropy["log_probs"]
1523	    log_probs = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0)
1524	    loss = -sum_of_sample_mean(log_probs)
1525	
1526	    # make sure the gradient could backprop correctly.
1527	    if log_probs.numel() == 0:
1528	        loss += 0 * logits.sum()

1531	        loss,
1532	        {
1533	            "loss": loss.clone().detach(),
1534	        },
1535	    )

# Data

## Training set — `openbmb/UltraData-RL-2609`, config `Math`

JustRL2 trains on the **Math** slice of
[UltraData-RL-2609](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openbmb/UltraData-RL-2609/tree/main/data/Math):
**32,412** competition- and textbook-style problems, each with a single extractable
answer verified against `ground_truth`. `python justrl2/prepare_data.py` downloads it
and writes `<data-dir>/UltraData-RL-Math-2609.jsonl`.

The Hub schema is five fields:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `uuid` | `Math_00001`-style id |
| `query` | the problem statement |
| `ground_truth` | the reference answer |
| `source` | provenance tag |
| `domain` | `Math` |

`prepare_data.py` adds `prompt` (= `query`) and `label` (= `ground_truth`) because that
is what miles reads (`--input-key prompt --label-key label`); the original columns are
kept as metadata. `prompt` goes through the model's chat template as a single user turn,
and responses are graded by miles' `math` reward (rule-based normalisation with
math-verify as a fallback).

### Why the difficulty distribution matters here

The dataset card documents that difficulty is calibrated **against the RL initialization
checkpoint** — the same [`openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model`](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model) this recipe starts from: items it
already solves at pass rate 1 are dropped (no gradient), the learnable band is kept, and
pass-rate-0 items with a confirmed-valid label are kept and left to online dynamic
sampling. That is why `DYNAMIC_SAMPLING=1` is part of the recipe: it discards
zero-variance groups at rollout time, so the remaining budget goes to problems that still
produce a learning signal. Labels are never modified by that filtering.

If you swap in your own corpus, the property to preserve is that one: drop what the
starting checkpoint already solves every time, keep the mixed band.

## Evaluation — AIME 2025 / 2026

The eval sets are public competition benchmarks and are **not** part of
UltraData-RL-2609, so they ship with this repo instead — 30 problems each, in the same
`prompt` / `label` format:

```
justrl2/data/aime-2025.jsonl
justrl2/data/aime-2026.jsonl
```

# JustRL2 — the method

JustRL2 is PPO for long-context (128k) math reasoning with a **separate critic that has no
language-model head**, a **mean-reward-seeded value head**, and a **length-adaptive GAE λ**.
This page explains each piece and points at the code; the full write-up with experiments
and ablations is the blog post [JustRL-II: Scaling Small LLMs to 128k Reasoning with a
Critic](https://panhaoxuan.notion.site/justrl-ii-scaling-small-llms-to-128k-reasoning-with-a-critic)

| `domain` | `Math` |

`prepare_data.py` adds `prompt` (= `query`) and `label` (= `ground_truth`) because that
is what miles reads (`--input-key prompt --label-key label`); the original columns are
kept as metadata. `prompt` goes through the model's chat template as a single user turn,
and responses are graded by miles' `math` reward (rule-based normalisation with
math-verify as a fallback).

### Why the difficulty distribution matters here

The dataset card documents that difficulty is calibrated **against the RL initialization
checkpoint** — the same [`openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model`](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/JustRL-II-base-model) this recipe starts from: items it
already solves at pass rate 1 are dropped (no gradient), the learnable band is kept, and
pass-rate-0 items with a confirmed-valid label are kept and left to online dynamic
sampling. That is why `DYNAMIC_SAMPLING=1` is part of the recipe: it discards
zero-variance groups at rollout time, so the remaining budget goes to problems that still
produce a learning signal. Labels are never modified by that filtering.

If you swap in your own corpus, the property to preserve is that one: drop what the
starting checkpoint already solves every time, keep the mixed band.

## Evaluation — AIME 2025 / 2026

The eval sets are public competition benchmarks and are **not** part of
UltraData-RL-2609, so they ship with this repo instead — 30 problems each, in the same
`prompt` / `label` format:

```
justrl2/data/aime-2025.jsonl
justrl2/data/aime-2026.jsonl
```

35	spends its first ~25 steps learning the offset *while the policy already updates against it*.
